description: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado): given how many strategy variants you tried (and how correlated they are), what Sharpe ratio would the *best of N* clear by luck alone, and does your actual strategy still clear that higher bar? Use when user asks "is my backtested Sharpe ratio real, or did I get lucky trying many variants?" or "how many independent trials does this really represent?". Provide either trial_sharpes[] (the N trials' own observed Sharpe ratios, most rigorous) or n_trials (+ optional avg_correlation to correct for correlated trials via Kish's design effect). Two limits to know. n_trials assumes the paper's illustrative case (trial Sharpes with mean 0 and variance 1, in per-period units), which is a very high bar for a low-frequency series: the threshold is about 1.6 at N=10, 2.5 at N=100 and 3.3 at N=1000, while a daily series has a per-period Sharpe of order 0.05, so dsr comes out effectively 0; use trial_sharpes there. trial_sharpes centers the threshold on the trials' own mean Sharpe plus their dispersion times the expected-maximum factor; this answers "does my strategy beat the best of N trials drawn from the spread I observed", not the zero-skill-null variant; pass null_mean true for that variant (mean fixed at 0, spread still taken from the trials); the two thresholds differ by exactly the trials' mean Sharpe. Returns: expected_max_sharpe (the luck-alone threshold), dsr (probability your strategy's true Sharpe exceeds it, 0-1), n_trials_effective.

avg_correlation.description: Average pairwise correlation between trials, 0-1 (default 0 = independent). Only used with n_trials; lowers the effective trial count via Kish's design effect.

n_trials.description: Number of strategy variants tried, if trial_sharpes were not tracked individually. Assumes trial Sharpes with mean 0 and variance 1 (per-period units): too strict for daily series, prefer trial_sharpes there.

null_mean.description: Only used with trial_sharpes. true = centre the luck threshold on 0 (zero-skill null) instead of on the trials' own mean Sharpe; the spread still comes from the trials. Default false.

returns.description: The candidate strategy's own return series

trial_sharpes.description: Observed Sharpe ratios of all N trials tried, if tracked. Takes priority over n_trials if both are given.
